messages.subject: Re: [seewave] RMS Value "Unit" or Scale
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I'm working on frogs advertisement calls descriptions and using seewave to plot clean calls.

My question is:  which is the correct scale to plot in the amplitude axes in my power spectrum plot?

If anyone can give me a hint here I'll be much appreciated!

please, find attached my R script and figure,

### Script###

require(seewave)

readWave("D:/Tesis/Anfibios PN CalileguaMB/Oreobates berdemenos/Advertisement_02b (1).WAV") -> O.berdemenos

layout(matrix(c(1,2,3,4,0,0),nc = 3, byrow = T),widths=c(6,3,1), heights = c(2.5,2.5,2.5,1.5))

par(mar=c(0.5,4,1,1))

spectro(O.berdemenos, flim = c(0,4),collevels = seq(-50,0,2), ovl = 85, scale = FALSE,axisX = FALSE,font.lab = 1, grid = FALSE)

spec(O.berdemenos, fft = 512, flim = c(0,4), font.lab=1, plot = 2, norm = FALSE, scale = TRUE)

par(mar=c(0.5,1,3,2))

dBscale(collevels = seq(-50,0,2),side=4, textlab="dB", cexlab=0.65, fontlab=1)

par(mar=c(4,4,0,1))

oscillo(O.berdemenos, bty="o", cexlab=0.65,fontlab=1, from = 0, to = 1.5)

cheers,

Martín

El jue., 23 de jul. de 2020 a la(s) 09:10, Jérôme SUEUR (jerome...@mnhn.fr) escribió:

> Calibration mainly refers to sound acquisition rather than to sound generation. I guess you can control the amplitude of the sounds you generate with SuperCollider and that afterwards you can control the SPL of the loudspeaker using a level meter.
> best
> Jerome
>
> De: "Liam Foley" <ltim...@gmail.com>
> À: "seewave GROUP" <see...@googlegroups.com>
> Envoyé: Mercredi 22 Juillet 2020 16:20:28
> Objet: Re: [seewave] RMS  Value "Unit" or Scale
>
> Thanks Jerome,
>
> The sounds I am looking at have all been synthesized within the same program SuperCollider. Knowing this how do I go about calibrating? Any info or resources appreciated.
>
> Thanks for the great package!
>
> On Wednesday, July 15, 2020 at 11:02:05 AM UTC-2:30, Jérôme SUEUR wrote:
> > Hello Liam,
> > The rms() function just computes the root-mean-square of any numeric vector. It has therefore no unit.
> > If you apply rms() on the envelope, which is not calibrated, you end up indeed with no calibrated data but you can still compare your rms values across different recordings, as soon as the recordings have been done in similar conditions (distance to the source, recording level etc).
> > HTH
> > Jerome
> >
> > De: "Liam Foley" <ltim...@gmail.com>
> > À: "seewave GROUP" <see...@googlegroups.com>
> > Envoyé: Mardi 14 Juillet 2020 14:31:26
> > Objet: [seewave] RMS  Value "Unit" or Scale
> >
> > Hello,
> >
> > I was wondering what unit or scale the value the RMS function returns is in. For example my code below..
> >
> >
> > soundrms<-rms(env(soundfile,plot=F))
> >
> > 1530924
> >
> > I used to get RMS values from the GUI based Amadeus sound editor, where RMS was in dB. I suspect the answer to this question is quite so simple, as it might have to be "calibrated".
> >
> > Thank you for your help.

messages.subject: Compare seewave::fund and tuneR::FF
messages.body_plain:
When using seewave::fund, it always seems to over-estimate the fundamental frequency, while tuneR:FF provides more accurate estimates. I would really like to use the seewave::fund version, because it provides a time series of fundamental frequency values, while tuneR::FF does not. Is this a known bias in seewave::fund?

A comparison of the two approaches is shown below.

# Simulate a 440Hz tuning fork
synth_440 <- seewave::synth(f = 44100,
                            d = 1,
                            cf = 440,
                            output = "Wave")

# Look at the frequency spectrum
f_spec <- seewave::fpeaks(spec = seewave::spec(wave = synth_440),
                          nmax = 2,
                          xlim = c(0, 1),
                          ylim = c(0, 1.1),
                          digits = 3)

# Use seewave::fund to calculate fundamental frequency
synth_fund <- seewave::fund(wave = synth_440,
                         plot = FALSE,
                         fmax = 500)
# Look at mean and median of fundamental frequency values
mean(synth_fund[, 2])
# [1] 0.4445222
median(synth_fund[, 2])
# [1] 0.4454545

# Compare with fundamental frequency calculation from tuneR::FF
synth_period <- tuneR::periodogram(object = synth_440)
synth_ff <- tuneR::FF(object = synth_period)
synth_ff
# [1] 439.9125

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Compare seewave::fund and tuneR::FF
messages.body_plain:
Dear ?,
synth:fund() and tuneR::FF() do not use the same processes. synth:fund() uses a cesptral approach when tuneR::FF() seems to use a peak search heuristic.
The cepstral approach works better for harmonic sounds (not pure tones as in your example). In addition in your example you use a 512 sample window for seewave:fund() (default setting)  but a 65536 sample window for tuneR::FF() (default setting).

Here is another test :

synth_440 <- seewave::synth(f = 44100,
                            d = 1,
                            cf = 440,

                            harmonics=c(1, 0.5, 0.2, 0.1),
                            output = "Wave")
## seewave

synth_fund <- seewave::fund(wave = synth_440,
                         plot = FALSE,
                         fmax = 500)

mean(synth_fund[, 2])
[1] 0.4432127
median(synth_fund[, 2])
[1] 0.441
## tuneR
synth_period <- tuneR::periodogram(object = synth_440, width=512)

synth_ff <- tuneR::FF(object = synth_period)

mean(synth_ff)
[1] 433.2245
median(synth_ff)
[1] 435.8465

I hope this helps a bit.

Best regards,

Jerome

De: "Jeff Oliver" <jeffrey...@gmail.com>
À: "seewave GROUP" <see...@googlegroups.com>
Envoyé: Jeudi 27 Août 2020 02:12:19

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Compare seewave::fund and tuneR::FF
messages.body_plain:
Great to know. The sounds we are ultimately going to be looking at are buzzes created by bees, which have harmonics, so it looks like seewave::fund() is going to be the best approach. We were trying to check our approach with pure (known) sounds from tuning forks, but this does not appear a fair comparison. Thanks again for the explanation.

Cheers,

Jeff
